newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan poll reveals dim view of South Korea.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan poll reveals dim view of South Korea.

text.p: As a dispute over Taiwan's plan to ship nuclear waste to North Korea intensifies, some 43 percent of Taiwan people revealed they disliked or detested nearby South Korea, a newspaper poll published on Sunday said.

The survey, conducted by the China Times newspaper on January 27 and 28, said 25 percent of the 870 people interviewed said their impression on South Korea was "not so good", while 18 percent said their impression was "very bad."
Only 15 percent held positive view on South Korea, the poll showed.
The respondents were not asked to give their views on the escalating nuclear waste row between Taipei and Seoul.
State-run Taiwan Power Co and a North Korean agency signed a contract to ship up to 200,000 barrels of nuclear waste to Pyongyang on January 11.
The Taipei-Pyongyang nuclear waste deal triggered militant protests in South Korea, which has expressed concerns about nuclear contamination on the Korean peninsula.
On Thursday, seven South Korean activists were deported by Taipei after clashing with supporters of the shipments outside Taiwan Power's headquarters.
Another South Korean anti-nuclear delegation, which includes four South Korean parliamentary deputies, arrived in Taiwan on Friday to press the government to cancel the deal.
Taiwan Vice-President Lien Chan has said his government would not intervene in the nuclear waste shipment, saying it was a lawful, safe business deal with no moral issue involved.
Taiwan has no diplomatic ties with either North Korea or South Korea, both of which recognise Taiwan's own rival -- the communist Chinese government in Beijing.
